title: Meadow vs. Cova: Which Dispensary POS Fits Your Operation?
summary: Meadow vs. Cova on eCommerce, pricing, payments, delivery, and G2 reviews: how the two dispensary POS platforms differ and which operations each one fits.
body_markdown:
Meadow and Cova are both cannabis POS platforms with Metrc integrations. The biggest difference is architecture: Cova pairs an in-store POS with partner tools and prices its eCommerce separately, while Meadow runs POS, delivery, eCommerce, loyalty, and compliance in one system on one flat monthly fee.


That difference shows up on the bill even if you never deliver. If you sell online for pickup or take debit, Cova prices its eCommerce separately and charges less on its plans only for stores that use Cova Pay. Delivery adds a partner on top of that.


**This Meadow vs. Cova comparison covers what each platform includes, how each is priced, how each handles payments and delivery, and what verified reviewers say about each, then lays out which operations each one fits.**

#### Key Takeaways


- Meadow runs POS, eCommerce, delivery, loyalty, and Metrc compliance in one system on one flat monthly fee per location, with no per-transaction fees.
- Meadow holds a 4.9 out of 5 rating on G2 to Cova's 4.6 as of November 2026, and in G2's head-to-head comparison reviewers score Meadow higher on ease of use, ease of setup, and quality of support.
- Cova prices its built-in eCommerce separately from its POS plans and charges less on those plans for stores that use Cova Pay, so compare quotes with online ordering and payments included.
- Delivery is native in Meadow, including hub-and-spoke and dynamic (ice cream truck) models, while Cova runs delivery fulfillment through partners such as Carrot and Breadstack.

## Meadow vs. Cova at a Glance


Cova is an in-store cannabis POS that connects to partner tools for delivery and CRM, while Meadow is an all-in-one platform built for dispensaries and delivery operators in Metrc states.


**Cova** sells its cannabis POS in three U.S. plan tiers and offers a built-in eCommerce product priced separately. Delivery fulfillment, CRM, and loyalty connect through partners such as Carrot, Breadstack, Alpine IQ, and Springbig. Cova integrates with Metrc and BioTrack and serves retailers in the U.S. and Canada. The trade-off is assembly: online ordering is its own line item, and a store that delivers runs at least one more vendor.


**Meadow** runs[POS](https://getmeadow.com/features/point-of-sale) , eCommerce, delivery, loyalty, SMS marketing, and Metrc compliance in one system, with one login, one inventory count, and one flat monthly fee per location. It serves operators in California, New York, New Jersey, Michigan, Massachusetts, and Minnesota.


**The short version:** if you operate in Canada or a BioTrack state, Cova covers markets Meadow doesn't. In Meadow's six states, one system on one bill is the simpler path, whether you run a single storefront or a delivery fleet.


For the full field, see[The Best Dispensary Point of Sale Systems for 2026](https://getmeadow.com/blog/best-dispensary-pos) .

## Questions to Ask as You Evaluate


Four questions separate Meadow and Cova faster than a feature list, so bring them to both demos.


### 1. What will the full quote include?


Ask each vendor to itemize what your store needs on day one: online ordering for pickup, loyalty, kiosks, payments, implementation, and hardware, plus delivery if it's on your roadmap. Then add the monthly cost of every partner tool you'd still need. Our[cannabis POS pricing guide](https://getmeadow.com/blog/cannabis-pos-pricing) breaks down how each pricing model adds up.


### 2. Does your plan price depend on your payment processor?


Some POS plans cost less when you use the vendor's own payment processing, which ties your software bill to one processor. Ask what the plan costs without it, and whether you can change processors later without repricing. Our guide to[accepting cashless payments at your dispensary](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-cashless-payments) covers the options.


### 3. Will you run delivery in the next two years?


Delivery is where Meadow and Cova differ most. Meadow runs delivery natively, while Cova's delivery fulfillment runs through a partner, which means a second contract and a second system for drivers. If delivery is on your roadmap, price that partner in now.


### 4. How many inventory counts will you reconcile?


Every channel that sells product, from the counter to the online menu to the delivery driver, should draw from the same count Metrc sees. Ask whether each channel reads one inventory or syncs between systems, and who fixes it when a sync fails. See[Metrc Reconciliation for Dispensaries](https://getmeadow.com/blog/metrc-reconciliation-for-dispensaries) for what a clean count takes.


For a full evaluation framework, see[The Complete Guide to Choosing a Cannabis Dispensary POS System](https://getmeadow.com/blog/guide-to-choosing-a-cannabis-dispensary-pos-system) .

## How Meadow and Cova Compare, Feature by Feature


Meadow and Cova both run the counter and integrate with Metrc, and they differ most on what the price includes: eCommerce, payments, delivery, and loyalty.


### eCommerce


Meadow and Cova both offer built-in online ordering. Cova prices its eCommerce separately from its Boutique and Powerhouse POS plans. Meadow's[eCommerce](https://getmeadow.com/features/ecommerce) and online menus are included in the platform fee, draw from the same inventory count as the sales floor, and come with Meadow SEO+, so menu pages are built to be found in search.


### Packaging and Pricing


Cova sells three U.S. plans, Boutique, Powerhouse, and Enterprise, tiered by the number of POS workstations, with Enterprise priced by quote. Built-in eCommerce is priced separately on the Boutique and Powerhouse plans, and both plans cost less with Cova Pay. Meadow charges[one flat monthly fee per location](https://getmeadow.com/pricing) that covers POS, eCommerce, delivery, loyalty, inventory, and compliance, with no per-transaction fees.


### Payments


Cova offers Cova Pay, and its Boutique and Powerhouse plans cost less for stores that use it, so your plan price depends on which processor you choose. Meadow supports[integrated PIN debit, wireless terminals, and eCommerce ACH](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-cashless-payments) , all connected to the POS, inventory, and Metrc, with no payment processor lock-in.


### Delivery


Delivery runs natively in Meadow, while Cova connects delivery fulfillment through partners.


Cova's eCommerce lets customers choose pickup or delivery at checkout. For fulfillment, Cova points delivery-focused retailers to integration partners such as Carrot and Breadstack. Carrot, a separate vendor, supplies the driver app, routing, and dispatch.


Meadow supports[hub-and-spoke, dynamic (ice cream truck), and hybrid delivery](https://getmeadow.com/features/cannabis-delivery) natively, with dispatch, tracking, customer communications, geofencing, and California delivery ledgers built in. In dynamic delivery, each vehicle operates as its own inventory location with its own menu.


### Marketing and Loyalty


Cova lists Alpine IQ and Springbig as its CRM and loyalty partners. Meadow includes built-in[loyalty and rewards](https://getmeadow.com/features/loyalty-and-rewards) and SMS marketing in the platform fee, and runs loyalty redemptions through the same discount engine as every other promotion.


### Compliance and Traceability


Meadow and Cova both integrate with Metrc. Meadow[connects directly to Metrc's API](https://getmeadow.com/features/metrc-compliance) , so every sale, adjustment, and delivery updates Metrc automatically, and Meadow's team monitors each store's Metrc sync to resolve errors before they become compliance risks. Adjustments and delivery ledgers happen inside Meadow, so staff open Metrc mainly to receive new deliveries.


Cova also supports BioTrack and serves Canadian retailers, which is the main reason operators outside Meadow's footprint consider it.

## Which Platform Fits Your Operation


Meadow fits storefronts and delivery operators in its six Metrc states that want one system, and Cova fits retailers in Canada and BioTrack states, which Meadow doesn't serve.


**Consider Cova if** you operate in Canada or a BioTrack state. The trade-off: eCommerce is priced separately, delivery fulfillment and CRM run through partners, and plan pricing is tied to Cova Pay, so budget for more line items as you add channels.


**Choose Meadow if:**


- You want online ordering, loyalty, and payments on one bill, with no per-transaction fees and your choice of processor.
- You want a POS your staff learns fast and support that answers in minutes.
- Delivery is a core channel, or will be, including dynamic (ice cream truck) delivery.
- You operate in California, New York, New Jersey, Michigan, Massachusetts, or Minnesota.


---


## One Platform vs. a Partner Stack


A partner stack costs more than its line items, because every added vendor brings its own contract, support line, login, and data sync.


- **One inventory count.** Every channel that sells product should draw from the count Metrc sees, with no sync in between.
- **One support line.** When an order stalls between two systems, someone has to own the fix.
- **One renewal.** Each partner contract renews, reprices, and changes on its own schedule.
- **A documented peak-day record.** Ask for uptime numbers and 4/20 history, in writing, for every system in the stack.


> **Having an all-in-one system with Meadow creates an ease of use that you can't get with having everything third party or having to use multiple companies to facilitate things, especially if they don't link on the backend; Meadow's made things really efficient for us having everything in one spot.**


Steven Murray, Marketing Director,[Coast to Coast](https://getmeadow.com/case-studies/coast-to-coast)

## Common Questions


### Is Meadow or Cova better for cannabis delivery?


Meadow is the stronger fit for most delivery operators in its six states. Delivery is native in Meadow, including hub-and-spoke, dynamic (ice cream truck), and hybrid models with dispatch, tracking, and geofencing built in. Cova offers delivery as a checkout option in its eCommerce and runs fulfillment through partners such as Carrot and Breadstack.


### How does Cova's pricing compare to Meadow's?


Cova sells three U.S. plan tiers based on the number of POS workstations, prices its built-in eCommerce separately, and charges less on its Boutique and Powerhouse plans for stores that use Cova Pay. Meadow charges one flat monthly fee per location that covers POS, eCommerce, delivery, loyalty, and compliance, with no per-transaction fees or processor lock-in.


### Can I switch from Cova to Meadow without downtime?


Yes. Meadow's onboarding team cleans up your Metrc data first, trains staff before go-live, and cuts over overnight, so you open the next morning on the new system. See[How to Switch Dispensary POS Without Losing a Day of Sales](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-pos-migration) for the full playbook.


### Does Meadow work in Canada or in BioTrack states?


No. Meadow integrates with Metrc and serves operators in California, New York, New Jersey, Michigan, Massachusetts, and Minnesota. Retailers in Canada or BioTrack states need a platform built for those markets, such as Cova.
